messages.author: 527e14923215b7e4
messages.subject: version 0.9-1 released
parts:
Greetings,

unmarked_0.9-1 was just submitted to CRAN and soon will be available for download on all platforms. Along with a few minor bug fixes, there are two important additions.

First, there is a new function, gdistsamp, to fit a generalized form of the Royle et al. (2004) distance sampling model. This expanded model relaxes the assumption that g(0)=1 by including an additional parameter psi, the probability of being available for detection. This should be useful for studies where cues such as bird songs or whale blows are counted. The gdistsamp function also allows abundance to be modeled using the negative binomial distribution. See Chandler et al. (Ecology 2011) for more details about this model.

The other new addition is a vignette on dynamic occupancy models (MacKenzie et al. 2003) . Marc Kéry deserves most of the credit for putting this together. Thanks Marc! In addition to helping with the implementation of colext(), this vignette describes many of unmarked's basic features such as data manipulation, prediction, model selection, etc...

More information about this release can be found here: https://sites.google.com/site/unmarkedinfo/home/release-notes

Richard

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] version 0.9-1 released
parts:
Dear all,

it was a pleasure to help write the vignette about colext(). Richard helped me with the code quite a bit (Thanks, Richard !) and for this, and also, especially, for developing the very useful unmarked package, I was happy to contribute something in exchange.

As you may see in this vignette, it contains a quite verbose description of the capabilities of colext. I think that having extensive worked examples is essential for letting many ecologists apply statistical analyses for their own data sets. In the longer term, it would be great to have such vignettes for all functions contained in unmarked. A little like Evan Cooch's MARK handbook. So perhaps some of you can have a try at writing something about their own favourite function in unmarked.

Thanks again, Richard (and Ian and Andy), for giving unmarked to the world.

Kind regards -- Marc
